clue.text: Old personnel carrier, powerfully armed?

parts.note: sounds like a military troop vehicle bristling with weapons, but means an enclosed seat of the past borne on poles by two strong-armed porters

explanation.surface: A vintage armoured troop transport bristling with heavy guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personnel carrier' and 'armed' suggest the army; the arms here are the bearers' brawny limbs, and the personnel is a single passenger.
explanation.definitionFit: This enclosed seat on poles carried one person through Georgian streets, lifted by two porters.

clue.text: Settle for unit out of capital

indicators.note: the letter for one is taken out of the name of the city

parts.note: Sofia is the capital of Bulgaria
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a housing unit outside the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle' looks like a verb; it is a wooden bench.
explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a long seat with a high back, a kind of couch.

clue.text: The main bass note, aurally

indicators.note: aurally means what is heard, so the phrase is spoken

parts.note: a bass note is deep, and C is a note, giving deep C

explanation.surface: A musical comment on the principal low note heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the poetic term for the ocean; 'deep C' spoken sounds just like it.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic name for the open ocean, whose far-down waters are this.

clue.text: Convertible omnibus on call, pound discount for careful drivers

indicators.note: convertible means able to be changed into another form, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A soft-top bus on call offers money off for safe motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convertible' looks like a car; it signals that OMNIBUS ON CALL, less one L for pound, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurers reduce premiums for motorists who make no insurance claims over a period.

clue.text: Where to cross beef cattle

definitions.meaning: read cryptically as 'here, a ford', a shallow place to cross a river
a red and white breed raised for meat

explanation.surface: A place to crossbreed animals for meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' suggests breeding cattle; it means fording a river. The breed is named after an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: This English county town gives its name to a red-and-white breed raised for meat, and splits into 'here' plus a river crossing.

clue.text: Lizard in the dark in Tennessee

parts.note: points to the playwright Tennessee Williams and his play The Night of the creature, the dark being night

explanation.surface: A reptile lurking at night in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennessee is not the state but the playwright Tennessee Williams, whose play is titled The Night of the ... with this lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tropical American reptile with a spiny crest down its back.

clue.text: A part of the garden not up yet

parts.note: a flower bed is a section of a garden

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that one flower patch has not yet sprouted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone still lying in bed is not up yet, an old word for 'in bed'.

clue.text: Post on island that keeps out cars

definitions.text: Post on island that keeps out cars

parts.words: Post on island that keeps out cars
parts.note: describes a short sturdy pillar set on a traffic island or at a road's end to stop vehicles

explanation.surface: Mail delivered to a car-free island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' and 'island' suggest mail to an isle; the island is in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A short thick upright stands on traffic islands and blocks vehicles from pedestrian areas.

clue.text: Madrid is in her itinerary, but part can be cut off

indicators.note: part says only a section of the words Madrid is in her itinerary is wanted

explanation.surface: Travel plans include Madrid, but some of the trip may be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude an heir from inheritance is to sever them from the family fortune.

clue.text: Where to find small jumper with a big top?

definitions.text: Where to find small jumper with a big top?

parts.words: Where to find small jumper with a big top?
parts.note: reads like asking where to buy a little sweater with a large collar, but the jumper is a tiny insect and the big top is a circus tent

explanation.surface: A shopper asks where to find a small sweater with an oversized top.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'jumper' is British for a sweater, the false trail; the real jumper is an insect performer, and a 'big top' is a circus tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny trained insects were once shown performing in miniature fairground shows under this name.

clue.text: Dole projections sound

indicators.note: the clue's last word tells us to take how the word for projections is spoken, in a non-rhotic British accent

parts.note: arms are limbs or parts that project from a body or chair

explanation.surface: A comment that benefit forecasts are reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dole' looks like unemployment pay and 'projections' like forecasts; in a non-rhotic British accent ARMS and ALMS are said almost alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To dole out is to hand out charity, and charitable handouts to the poor are given this old name.

clue.text: Debasement in a late Tudor building

indicators.note: building means putting the letters together into a new structure

explanation.surface: Decay found in an old sixteenth-century house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun for a Tudor house; it rearranges IN A LATE TUDOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something impure by mixing in inferior substances lowers its quality.

clue.text: Minor addition to this land mass in Turkey

definitions.text: Minor addition to this land mass in Turkey

parts.words: Minor addition to this land mass in Turkey
parts.note: adding the word Minor after the continent's name gives the classical name of the Anatolian peninsula, which lies in Turkey

explanation.surface: A small extension of territory in the country of Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor addition' seems to mean a small extra; it is literally the word Minor added to the answer, naming Anatolia.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest continent, whose westernmost peninsula, Anatolia, was called by its name plus Minor.

clue.text: Tied after penalty — very nice indeed!

indicators.note: the word for tied comes after the word for penalty

parts.note: a fine is a monetary penalty
a drawn match is one where the scores are tied

explanation.surface: Excitement at a team escaping with a draw after being punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' here is the old sense of precise or subtle, not pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely subtle or delicately precise is drawn out very fine, which is nice in its old sense of exacting.

clue.text: Mark on tongue a disease produced

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
tongue means language, here Latin

explanation.surface: A spot on the tongue caused by an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like the body part; it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet fever, a bacterial infection with a red rash, goes by this other name.

clue.text: Hanger for lute is extra

parts.note: lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints
more means additional or extra

explanation.surface: A peg to hang a stringed instrument on is surplus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanger' looks like a peg; it is an old short sword, and 'lute' is a sealing clay, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger is a short sword once hung from the belt, and this is a Scottish broadsword.

clue.text: Second shelf for the hammer

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A spare shelf on which to keep the hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is short for a sledgehammer, a heavy long-handled tool for smashing.

clue.text: Sort of rider who puts nothing on a horse

definitions.text: Sort of rider who puts nothing on a horse

parts.words: Sort of rider who puts nothing on a horse
parts.note: sounds like a punter placing no bet, but means riding with no saddle placed on the horse

explanation.surface: A jockey type who never bets on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts nothing on' suggests betting; it means no saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a horse without a saddle is this style.

clue.text: Charges kept down by this disciplinarian

definitions.meaning: a muzzle-loading gun's powder charge is pushed and held down the barrel with a rod
a strict, rigid enforcer of rules

explanation.surface: A strict officer keeps his charges in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like people in someone's care; it is the gun's explosive load.
explanation.definitionFit: The rod for tamping a musket's load gave its name to a rigidly strict person.

clue.text: What a relief, to celebrate boisterously!

definitions.meaning: refers to the relief of Mafeking in 1900 during the Boer War, which set off wild street celebrations

explanation.surface: A sigh of relief, then wild celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb comes from Mafeking, a South African town whose relief from siege in 1900 brought crowds onto London's streets.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb was coined from the jubilant London crowds after a siege in the Boer War was lifted.

clue.text: How to proceed when you get your sea-legs?

definitions.text: How to proceed when you get your sea-legs?

parts.words: How to proceed when you get your sea-legs?
parts.note: sea-legs normally means steadiness aboard ship, but here it suggests literal legs for gliding over the sea, long boards strapped to the feet

explanation.surface: Advice for a new sailor on what to do once steady aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea-legs' is the idiom for balance on a rolling deck; read literally, they are boards towed across the waves behind a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding over the water on long boards, pulled by a motorboat, is a sport using these.

clue.text: Display little enterprise in the theatrical profession

parts.note: a show is a display
biz is a shortened word for business, an enterprise

explanation.surface: Showing little initiative in the world of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little enterprise' looks like lack of initiative; it is a short form of business.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment as an industry, the stage and screen world, is informally called this.

clue.text: It 'would be crazy to black this fruit

indicators.note: the clue says adding black to the answer would give the word for crazy, so black is removed from that word

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy
B is an abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it mad to blacklist a certain fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' looks like a verb meaning boycott; it is the letter B, which added to the answer makes BANANAS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French and botanical name for the pineapple.

clue.text: Wealth — a key to power

parts.note: F is a musical key
fluence is colloquial for influence or a mesmeric power, as in putting the fluence on someone

explanation.surface: A remark that money unlocks power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluence' is an informal British word for influence or hypnotic power.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperity and abundant riches are the condition described.

clue.text: A reversing test — very little to it

indicators.note: the word for the test is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: A driving test in reverse gear is not much to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversing' looks like part of a driving test; it turns MOT, the British vehicle safety check, into TOM.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest particle of an element, figuratively a tiny amount, as in 'not an atom of truth'.

clue.text: Hairstyle variations for the pool

definitions.meaning: a permanent wave set into the hair
on British football pools coupons, a permutation covers several combinations of matches

explanation.surface: Different hairstyles for a swimming session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The pool' looks like a swimming pool; it is the British football pools, a betting game on match results.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasting chemically set wave in hair, and a short form of permutation on a pools coupon.

clue.text: I turn handle to raise the flag

indicators.note: the title for a knight is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: a handle is slang for a title such as Sir

explanation.surface: Someone cranks a handle to hoist the flag up a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' and 'flag' suggest a flagpole; a handle is a title, and the yellow flag is a wild plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild waterside plant of this genus with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Greedy in a bestial frenzy

indicators.note: a wild frenzy throws the letters of 'a bestial' into disorder

explanation.surface: A glutton eating like a frenzied animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frenzy' rearranges A BESTIAL into SATIABLE, which follows IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone never satisfied, always wanting more, is grasping.

clue.text: Khan collected Egyptian cross

indicators.note: the letters of the name are gathered up and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A Khan acquired an ancient Egyptian cross for his collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' rearranges the letters of KHAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This looped cross was the ancient Egyptian symbol of life.

clue.text: German Jews shake off National Socialist master

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of shake have gone wrong and are rearranged

parts.note: Nazi is short for National Socialist
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: German Jews throw off the domination of a Nazi master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SHAKE into ASHKE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name for Jews of central and eastern European descent, originally from the Rhineland.
